Stage helpers now read the writer and model settings in effect at spawn time, so changing a model in settings applies to the next pm-read spawn. The typecheck passes, and so does the new test file. The changed paths are all inside `owns_paths`:

- `src/rooms/core/server/stage-settings.ts` (new) and `src/rooms/core/server/index.ts` (export)
- `src/rooms/critique/server/critique-runs.ts`
- `src/rooms/memory/server/memory.ts`
- `src/rooms/docs/server/docs.ts`
- `src/rooms/project-life/server/onboarding.ts`
- `src/rooms/project-life/server/project-life.ts`
- `src/rooms/writer/server/start.ts` and `src/rooms/writer/server/sticky.ts`
- `tests/stage-helper-live-settings.test.ts` (new)

**Root cause.** The stage helpers read the project's settings rows directly, with `loadProjectSettings` (`src/rooms/storage/database.ts:848`). That skips the «Общие настройки» layer in `defaults:v1`, which holds the global writer choice. The writer spawn sees that layer through `effectiveProjectSettings` (`src/rooms/writer/server/spawn.ts:151`). The pm-read fallback then reached the run's frozen `config.writerProviderId` (`src/rooms/critique/server/critique-runs.ts:41` before the change). That explains the owner's Gemini result: the global writer was switched to claude-code, but pm-read still used the snapshot.

**Fix.** `stageHelperSettings` (`src/rooms/core/server/stage-settings.ts`) layers the run's scopes and rows over the saved global writer defaults. It does not use `effectiveProjectSettings` or `inheritProjectValues`, because those inject a codex writer when no selection exists. That would replace the run snapshot and break the "previous source when absent" invariant. Every owned stage helper now uses it: pm-read, plan critique, code critique, specialist, memory, onboarding, project-life, and docs. Code critique's `frozenPolicy` is still used for recovery of the same critique round. It is not the spawn-time read.

**Sticky writer: retired.** `hotWriter` takes the current writer selection, computed the same way as the writer spawn. If the area's thread reports another provider or model, the task gets a fresh writer. An unknown model keeps the thread. This relies on `threads.defaultExecutionOptions` reporting the model the thread was spawned with.

**Verification.**
- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `tests/stage-helper-live-settings.test.ts`: 6 pass. The owner case (snapshot A, global default B, new pm-read spawn gets B) fails when I temporarily restore the old row-only behaviour. I did not check the sticky tests against the old code.
- 49 related existing test files: 473 pass, 1 skipped.
- I did not run the full suite.

**Not done.**
- `src/rooms/night/server/night.ts` and `src/rooms/workflow/server/workflow-step-executors.ts` have the same raw-settings pattern. They are outside `owns_paths`, so I left them.
- I could not reproduce the owner's exact hub database state. The fix is based on the code path, not on that data.

dispatchContext.memoryText:
- Writer skill picking lives in `src/rooms/writer/server/skill-pick.ts` and runs before writer spawn. It uses Jev with a 15 s deadline, caches the catalog for 10 min and skill kinds in plugin KV, and respects `writer.skill_pick` (default on). Picks and task skill hints are passed through `ExtraAccess` and recorded in the attempt dispatch context for code-repair reads in `finish.ts`. The Jev picker in `packages/jev/src/judgments/skill-pick.ts` uses a 0.3 threshold and returns at most five catalog skills. Task-v2 accepts up to eight optional skill hints.
- Settings applicability data classifies `writer.skill_pick` (s474) as editable in the OWN channel, with evidence at `src/rooms/writer/server/skill-pick.ts:115`.
- `src/rooms/core/server/pm-spawn.ts` sends a caller-named service tier when provider lookup fails or returns no provider. It strips the tier when the provider explicitly reports no tiers; an unnamed spawn with unknown tier support sends no tier.
